newsitem.title: USA: TWA Q3 hurt by cancellations, lost bookings.
newsitem.headline: TWA Q3 hurt by cancellations, lost bookings.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc, reporting a loss of $14.3 million for the third quarter, cited an unusually high level of domestic flight cancellations and the loss of some premium fare bookings.
Flight cancellations were partly the result of an extremely aggressive growth plan for summer flying, which caused unanticipated expenses and the loss of some revenue, TWA said.
It said its yield in the quarter suffered, in part due to the loss of premium fare bookings following the crash of TWA Flight 800 on July 17.

Jeffrey Erickson, TWA president, said in a statement the company was disappointed with its third quarter. The results follow "six consecutive quarters of year-over-year improvement in operating earnings," he said.
"The events of the summer of 1996 have dealt us a setback," he said. "We will redouble our efforts through the remainder of this year and into 1997 to put our rebuilding effort back on track."
As reported earlier, summer traffic, load factors and overall revenues exceeded 1995 levels. However, domestic yield was below the 1995 level in July and August and was flat in September.
International yields for all three months of the third quarter were below 1995 levels.

TWA also said a fall-off in advance bookings following the crash of Flight 800, resulting in reduced load factor. This decline reverves a year-to-date trend of increases in load factor, the airline said.
The company said it believes this drop in bookings is consistent with the experience of other airlines that have suffered similar tragedies.
TWA said its fuel expense for the third quarter was $162.4 million, up from $122.1 million a year ago

Maintenance materials and repairs expense for the third quarter was $53.5 milion, up $23.3 million from a year ago.The company said it is making significant expenditures to enhance maintenance to, among other things, improve schedule reliability.
Regarding its flying plan, which was expanded this summer, TWA said it adjusted September and subsequent schedules for a more manageable level of flying and to improve operational performance.
As a result, on-time performance improved to 75.6 percent in September from 67.7 percent in August. October on-time performance thus far is 75.8 percent.
